Welcome. Take a moment and imagine this: what if, instead of feeling weighed down by all the things you own, you could find real clarity and freedom just beneath the surface? You know, we’re told that having more—more stuff, more status, more distractions—will make us happier, but how often does the opposite happen? That’s the heart of what Joshua Becker explores in his book, The More of Less: Finding the Life You Want Under Everything You Own. He invites us to look beyond the promise of comfort that possessions seem to offer, and instead, consider the true cost of excess—the way it can quietly erode our sense of purpose and joy.
As we dive into this journey together, we’ll discover that minimalism isn’t just about tidying up or getting rid of stuff. It’s about making space—space for deeper relationships, for creativity, and for real personal growth. When we start letting go of what we don’t need, new possibilities begin to unfold. We realize that our things can either help us reach our dreams, or hold us back from living them.
So, if you’ve ever wondered what life might look like with a little less clutter and a lot more meaning, you’re in the right place. Together, let’s explore how embracing minimalism can lead us to a life that’s not just simpler, but richer and more fulfilling than we ever expected.
